hook: Apple's *$299* Smart Hub Takes On Amazon, Google
dek: HomeView is Apple's new smart home hub with a screen, Siri, and FaceTime.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Apple unveiled HomeView, a *$299* smart home hub with a screen. Preorders open today, ships Nov. 13.

slides.label: The device
slides.text: It's a cuboid version of the HomePod with a *7-inch display*, sold in countertop or wall-mount versions.

slides.label: No phone needed
slides.text: HomeView runs Calendar, Messages, FaceTime, Photos, Music, and more, so you can *skip your phone*.

slides.label: Smart dashboard
slides.text: It also works as a *smart home dashboard*: ask Siri to check cameras, adjust the thermostat, lock doors.

slides.label: New accessories
slides.text: Apple also launched a smart *deadbolt lock*, security cameras, and a doorbell alongside HomeView.

slides.label: Knows who you are
slides.text: HomeView can recognize up to *six people* in a household and personalize the screen for each one.

slides.label: The real fight
slides.text: Apple is now going head to head with Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub after HomePod's rocky run.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: Why it matters: when Big Tech opens a new platform, underrepresented hardware makers and developers get in early.

cta_line: The *smart home* wars just got real.
question: HomeView or Echo Show? Pick one.
first_comment: Fun fact: Apple's rumored next version could have a robotic arm that moves the screen to follow you.

caption_instagram:
Apple just dropped HomeView, its new $299 smart home hub with a screen, taking direct aim at Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub.

The device looks like a cuboid HomePod with a 7-inch display up front. It runs apps like Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Photos, and Music right on the screen, so you're not always reaching for your phone. It also doubles as a smart home dashboard, letting Siri control your cameras, thermostat, lights, and locks. Apple dropped new smart home accessories too: a deadbolt lock, security cameras, and a doorbell.

The wildest part? HomeView can recognize up to six different people in your house and personalize the screen for whoever walks up. Preorders are open now, shipping November 13, per TechCrunch.

HomeView or Echo Show? Pick one.

caption_linkedin:
Apple officially entered the smart display race this week with HomeView, a $299 hub built to compete directly with Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub.

The device runs Apple's core apps (Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Photos, Music) on a 7-inch screen, and uses Apple's updated Siri to control thermostats, lights, locks, and cameras. Apple paired the launch with new smart home hardware: a deadbolt lock, security cameras, and a doorbell, signaling a bigger ecosystem play, not just one device.

One standout feature: HomeView can recognize up to six people in a household and personalize the screen for each person automatically, a detail that hints at where consumer AI hardware is headed next.

For founders and operators building in hardware, smart home, or AI interfaces, Apple re-entering this category resets the competitive map and opens new integration opportunities for smaller players willing to move fast, per TechCrunch.

Will Apple finally crack the smart home market? Yes or no.
